one_line_reason: No shortlisted trial compares oral Fo-Ti/Polygonum multiflorum against a true placebo alone, and this identity's own shortlist includes strong, repeated hepatotoxicity warnings for this exact herb.

selected.population: Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease (n=209 total: 120 compound-extract group, 60 Polygonum multiflorum-extract-alone group, 29 western-medicine control)
selected.intervention: Polygonum multiflorum extract alone (Chinese herb control arm), oral, 12 weeks
selected.primary_outcome: MMSE and ADL scores; overall therapeutic effective rate
selected.why_selected: the only shortlisted record with any outcome data for Polygonum multiflorum (Fo-Ti) extract used largely on its own (as a comparator arm, effective rate 73.33%), though the study's main positive finding belongs to a separate 'compound' extract group, and there is no placebo control or described blinding.

blockers: No shortlisted trial compares oral Fo-Ti/Polygonum multiflorum extract against a true placebo; the only outcome data available (20622335) is from a three-active-arm comparison with no blinding described, and the study's main positive result belongs to a 'compound' extract, not Fo-Ti alone.

This identity's own shortlist includes a systematic review of herb-induced liver injury (30639232) naming Polygonum multiflorum as one of the leading causes of hepatotoxic reactions among herbal products — a serious safety concern that should be weighed heavily against any efficacy claim.
A comprehensive toxicology review (25449462) also documents hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and embryonic toxicity associated with this plant's quinone compounds (emodin, rhein).

handoff_pmids.note: Systematic review of herb-induced liver injury (HILI) across 31 studies; Polygonum multiflorum is named among the main herbs implicated, with HILI skewing toward hepatocellular injury and being more common in women.

Comprehensive review of Polygonum multiflorum's botany, pharmacology, and toxicology; documents hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and embryonic toxicity attributed to quinone compounds (emodin, rhein) alongside its purported therapeutic uses.

excluded_pmids.reason: Narrative review of TSG (a Polygonum multiflorum compound) anti-aging mechanisms, mostly preclinical; explicitly states standardized systems for evaluating clinical efficacy are still needed.
Historical bencao (materia medica) textual investigation of Heshouwu's origin and processing; not clinical trial data.

RCT of a 9-ingredient multi-ingredient 'fat-loss' product (Fo-Ti is one of nine, including caffeine and yohimbine); effect cannot be isolated to Fo-Ti, and overall results were largely non-significant between conditions.

RCT of a multi-herb formula (astragalus, Polygonum multiflorum, Pyrrosia) combined with a pharmaceutical drug (Tripterygium wilfordii) for chronic kidney disease; a combination product with a drug, not isolated Fo-Ti.
RCT of a 6-herb Crataegus-based combination formula for dyslipidemia, with Polygonum multiflorum as one ingredient; effect cannot be isolated to Fo-Ti alone.
